data.events: Post Induction Thanksgiving Service of the Lay Chairman, Bro. Eric Sasu Somuah
data.sermonTopic: Preparing for His Coming
data.worshipHighlights: The worship service was vibrant, with community members dressed in traditional kente attire. The church members wore their kente dresses to show support for their brother, who is part of the congregation. He spoke about the importance of Advent and emphasized why Christians should take it seriously. Advent encompasses the four Sundays leading up to Christmas, with each Sunday focusing on a specific theme, represented by the four candles of Advent: Hope, Peace, Joy, and Love. He urged the congregation to live well with everyone, especially during this time as Christians. Our lives should shine brightly to those outside the community and draw them in.

data.events: Induction of New Leaders And Appreciation Of Outgoing Leaders.
data.sermonTopic: CALLED AND ANOINTED FOR PURPOSE
data.worshipHighlights:
The outgoing stewards were presented with service awards. Sis. Adraiana Hammond (Steward Welfare), Bro. Benjamin Kwofie (Finance), and Bro. George Oduro (Admin) were among those honoured. Additionally, plaques were awarded to members who went above and beyond in their sacrifices for the church.

The following brothers received awards for guaranteeing the manse: Bro. Jacob Kumi and Bro. Peter Kumah, who now resides in Ghana. Other plaques were awarded to brothers and sisters who used their personal property to secure the mortgage for our church at 69 Milvan Drive, North York. The recipients included Mrs. Benjamin Kwofie, Mrs. Elizabeth Kwofie, Mr. Charles Kwofie, Mrs. Catherine Kwofie, Mrs. Eric Sasu Somuah, Sis. Vera Somuah, Dr. David Lartey, and Sis. Alberta Lartey. They were recognized and appreciated for their dedicated service to the church.

data.sermonTopic: Turning Towards the Promise: Repentance as a Journey Of Faith
Turning Towards the Promise: Repentance as a journey of Faith.
data.worshipHighlights: It is Abraham walking before God, receiving a new name, trusting in a promise his body could not support. It is Paul being pressed and perplexed, yet not losing heart, fixing his eyes on the eternal and saying 'I believe.' It is the disciple who hears Jesus' call to self-denial and, choosing to lose the life of self-sufficiency, finds the life that is truly life.
